people: Western Han historian, author of the Shiji, cited here for its Treatise on Pitch Standards (Lü shu)

claims.event: Cited as author of the Treatise on Pitch Standards (律書) on the numbers of the fifth and sixth degrees [External dating, inferred: Approximate floruit of Sima Qian, author of the Shiji (completed c. 91 BC); the chapter only cites his treatise, so the date is contextual.]

translationRepairs: The lü section below adopts the seven-tone framework with tonic as foundation: when Huangzhong serves as tonic, the string's tonic part answers to Huangzhong, the second to Taicu, the third to Guxian, altered fourth to Ruibin, fifth to Yize, sixth to Wushe, and altered leading tone to half Huangzhong.

The Lülü houbian (Sequel to the Correct Meaning of the Pitch Pipes) adopts the seven-tone framework with tonic as foundation: when Huangzhong serves as tonic, the string's tonic part answers to Huangzhong, the second to Taicu, the third to Guxian, altered fourth to Ruibin, fifth to Yize, sixth to Wushe, and altered leading tone to half Huangzhong.
律呂后編 is the title of the Qing imperial sequel compilation on pitch pipes, not "the lü section below"
